posts.text: chatgpt for building interactive educational tools

quotedTweet.text:
Only if education could be this interactive ❤️‍🔥

I've had a looong wish to build something genuinely useful through vibe coding, and I finally did it. 

A 3D human anatomy application built with @threejs using GPT 5.6 Sol. 

It all started with a single design image that I created using GPT Image 2.0. I then used it to generate every 3D organ image, one by one.

Next, I converted each of those images into 3D models using @tripoai (and no, they didn't sponsor this 😄).

After that, I opened Codex, wrote a master prompt based on the design, and gave it the prompt, the design image, and all the 3D models.

Codex built the first version beautifully, but there was one big problem. 

Every single 3D model was nearly 120-150 MB. That obviously wasn't practical for the web and was giving a performance of 16fps.

After a few iterations, Codex optimized each model down to roughly 2–5.5 MB while preserving the visual quality, reducing the total asset size from ~900 MB to just 28.6 MB. And each model loads on demand. 

Along the way, Codex also generated those anatomical illustrations showing where each organ sits in the human body, and even created the interactive hotspot markers that explain different parts of every organ. It handled all of that.

The process wasn't exactly one shot, but it also wasn't difficult. You just have to do it step by step. 

It genuinely felt like building something that could make learning anatomy much more engaging.

The inspiration came from @DilumSanjaya's 3D animal plant cell project. I remember seeing it and thinking, "I want to build something like this one day." 

And I did it :D

Live: https://t.co/gIFgkj8UVB
Code: https://t.co/nijvyWcyxO
quotedTweet.translationZh:
要是教育也能这么互动就好了 ❤️‍🔥

我一直很想通过 vibe coding 做出真正有用的东西，现在终于做到了。

这是一个用 @threejs 和 GPT 5.6 Sol 构建的 3D 人体解剖应用。

一切都始于我用 GPT Image 2.0 创建的一张设计图。然后我用它逐个生成了每个 3D 器官图像。

接着，我用 @tripoai 把这些图像转换成 3D 模型（他们真的没有赞助我 😄）。

之后，我打开 Codex，根据设计写了一份主提示词，并把提示词、设计图和所有 3D 模型都交给它。

Codex 很漂亮地构建出了第一个版本，但有一个大问题。

每个 3D 模型都接近 120-150 MB。这显然不适合网页，性能只有 16fps。

经过几轮迭代，Codex 在保留视觉质量的同时，把每个模型优化到约 2–5.5 MB，将总资源大小从约 900 MB 降到仅 28.6 MB。而且每个模型都会按需加载。

在这个过程中，Codex 还生成了那些显示各个器官在人体中位置的解剖插图，甚至创建了交互式热点标记，用来解释每个器官的不同部位。这些它全都处理了。

这个过程并不是一次完成，但也不难。你只需要一步一步来。

这真的让我感觉自己做出了一个能让解剖学习更有趣的东西。

灵感来自 @DilumSanjaya 的 3D 动物植物细胞项目。我记得当时看到它时就在想：“总有一天我也要做一个这样的东西。”

然后我做到了 :D

Code: https://t.co/nijvyWcyxO

posts.text: Worth noting that to this day, base LLMs (no test time compute) *still* perform poorly on the ARC 1 benchmark from 2019 (on unseen tasks) despite continued massive scaling (~100,000x since 2019). We can say that without the switch to the test-time compute paradigm, AI would still not be capable of the kind of advanced reasoning that sota systems display today. Scaling the single-pass, static, next-token prediction paradigm of the GPT-2 through GPT-4 era was running into a capability asymptote. To bypass this plateau, test-time adaptation was a necessary evolutionary step.

posts.translationZh: 值得注意的是，直到今天，基础 LLM（没有测试时计算）在 2019 年的 ARC 1 基准上（面对未见过的任务）表现仍然很差，尽管规模持续大幅扩大（自 2019 年以来约 100,000 倍）。可以说，如果没有转向测试时计算范式，AI 仍无法具备当今 sota 系统展现出的那种高级推理能力。GPT-2 到 GPT-4 时代那种单次前向、静态、下一个 token 预测范式的扩展，已经逼近能力渐近线。要突破这个平台期，测试时适应是必要的演进步骤。

posts.text:
借用心理学「系统一 / 系统二」的说法，AI 正在形成一种很有意思的能力结构：

它可以解决极其复杂的数学问题，也会在看似简单的常识题上翻车。

数学和代码更接近「系统二」：步骤明确，可以反复推演，也容易验证。AI 在这类任务上的进步非常快。

真正难补的，反而是「系统一」依赖的直觉、常识和情境判断。很多人类不假思索就能理解的事情，可能才是 AI 最难学会的。

posts.text: @GaryMarcus is right.  Cognition is uneven.  But there’s a positive take to be had too. It is precisely the non-unformity of cognition that opens space for AI that can genuinely complement/amplify human cognition, rather than replace it (as the AGI narrative implies)

quotedTweet.text:
The “AGI-is-near” community keeps committing the same logical fallacy over and over; I have seen it at least half a dozen times today alone. Every time there’s an advance, I see the same error.

Here’s how the fallacy works.

1. Someone pretends that all cognition is created equally. (Totally untrue.)

2. Whenever AI achieves success on some form of (fancy) cognition they want you to believe that success on all forms of AI is imminent.   

I include three prominent examples from today below, each promising that some grand universal can be solved (“science”, “every discipline”, “every problem [people] face in life”), simply because there was an advance in a particular domain (today, math, other times coding, etc).

You don’t have to be a cognitive psychologist to realize that this inference just doesn’t follow. We all know that expertise in math doesn’t guarantee genius in all domains.

We all know, for example, people who are great at math or physics or programming but struggle with writing or understanding human relationships (and conversely great writers who are weak at math), etc. 

It’s common to be good at some forms of cognition and not others. Expertise in one domain does not at all guarantee expertise in all or even most domains.

That’s precisely *why* people like Gardner and Sternberg developed multidimensional theories of intelligence, why the SAT tests math separately from verbal, etc.

Astra is (apparently - we still haven’t seen the methodology) great at math, or at least some forms of math, but that does not mean that it will avoid hallucinations or solve the reliability problems other GenAI systems have. It doesn’t even mean it will be able to read a PDF properly.  It doesn’t mean it will be able to follow hard rules either. (Which should terrify you.)

In fact, the performance we saw today doesn’t even mean it can write a decent math proof; to the contrary, the mathematician @henryquantum has already given an example where clarity in the proof was lacking.

Whatever you do, please don’t get suckered into the “all cognition is alike” fallacy. It’s not  all alike. 

Astra is obviously good at some problems; but that doesn’t mean it will be good at problems that are hard to formalize. It doesn’t mean it will be magic. It doesn’t mean it’s AGI or ASI or any of that. 

It’s *very* impressive. But I see no reason whatsoever to think it is AGI let alone ASI. If it can score even a 5/10 on my 2024 bet with Miles Brundage I will be surprised.

Enough with this fallacy.
quotedTweet.translationZh:
“AGI 即将到来”群体一再犯同一个逻辑谬误；光是今天我就至少见过六次。每当有进展出现，我都会看到同样的错误。

这个谬误是这样运作的。

1. 有人假装所有认知都是一样的。（完全不对。）

2. 每当 AI 在某种（高级）认知形式上取得成功，他们就想让你相信，AI 在所有形式上的成功都近在眼前。

我在下面列出今天的三个典型例子，它们都承诺某个宏大的普遍目标可以被解决（“科学”、“每个学科”、“[人们]生活中面对的每个问题”），仅仅因为某个特定领域取得了进展（今天是数学，其他时候是编程等）。

你不必是认知心理学家也能意识到，这种推论根本站不住脚。我们都知道，数学专长并不能保证在所有领域都是天才。

例如，我们都认识一些数学、物理或编程很强，但在写作或理解人际关系方面吃力的人（反过来也有数学薄弱的优秀作家），等等。

擅长某些认知形式而不擅长另一些，是很常见的。一个领域的专长完全不能保证在所有甚至大多数领域都有专长。

这正是 Gardner 和 Sternberg 等人提出多维智能理论的原因，也是 SAT 将数学和语文分开测试的原因，等等。

Astra（显然——我们还没看到方法论）很擅长数学，或至少某些形式的数学，但这并不意味着它会避免幻觉，或解决其他 GenAI 系统存在的可靠性问题。甚至不意味着它能正确读取 PDF。也不意味着它能遵循严格规则。（这应该让你感到害怕。）

事实上，我们今天看到的表现甚至不意味着它能写出一篇像样的数学证明；相反，数学家 @henryquantum 已经给出一个例子，说明其证明缺乏清晰性。

无论如何，请不要被“所有认知都一样”的谬误骗了。它们并不都一样。

Astra 显然擅长某些问题；但这并不意味着它会擅长难以形式化的问题。不意味着它是魔法。不意味着它是 AGI 或 ASI 或诸如此类的东西。

它非常令人印象深刻。但我完全看不出有什么理由认为它是 AGI，更不用说 ASI 了。如果它能在我 2024 年与 Miles Brundage 的赌约中拿到哪怕 5/10，我都会感到惊讶。

别再犯这个谬误了。

posts.translationZh: 模型通常不用测试时训练，而是在 token 空间里做测试时搜索。它们实际上是在测试时进行自然语言程序合成。如今的模型会使用海量测试时计算，我们早已不再处于过去那种单次前向传播、预测下一个 token 答案的范式。

posts.text: To address the limits of deep learning and avoid stalling, the field of AI started by applying patch (1), which started being demoed 9 months later in December 2024 and has now become completely ubiquitous. However, long term, it is simply inevitable that AI will move to patch (2).

quotedTweet.text:
There are essentially two main options to remedy this: 

1. Find ways to perform active inference, so that the model adapts its learned program in contact with a new data distribution at test time. Would likely lead to some meaningful progress, but it isn't the ultimate solution, more of an incremental improvement. 

2. Change the training mechanism to something more robust than SGD, such as the MDL principle. This would pretty much require moving away from deep learning (curve fitting) altogether and embracing discrete program search instead (which I have advocated for many years as a way to tackle reasoning problems...)
quotedTweet.translationZh:
本质上有两个主要办法可以补救：

1. 寻找进行主动推理的方法，让模型在测试时接触新的数据分布时调整其学到的程序。这可能会带来一些有意义的进展，但不是最终解决方案，更像是渐进式改进。

2. 将训练机制换成比 SGD 更稳健的东西，比如 MDL 原则。这基本上需要彻底离开深度学习（曲线拟合），转而采用离散程序搜索（多年来我一直主张用这种方式解决推理问题……）

分享一个小技巧：在 @openai codex 里，你可以 @ 一个线程并把这个 @ 排进队列，所以如果你的项目被某个平台功能卡住了，你实际上可以预先推进项目，让它在平台解锁后继续进行。

当然了……在整个过程中，我其实并不是严格必要的。所以一个更好的 multiagent harness 会在平台和项目之间无缝来回编排工作……只是这不是一个很常见的用例，除非你真的在构建一个平台（大多数人并不是；大多数人只是基于平台构建应用，或者构建一个只有 1 个产品/应用租户的小平台）。

I know it feels very tempting to dunk, and that's fair, but to be clear, my past criticism of base LLMs does not apply to TTA systems, in the same way that criticism of the limits of steam trains would not apply to current-day electrified bullet trains (even if they feel similar and use the same platform, the principles at work are substantially different). I have first updated my views in December 2024 -- by that point I no longer believed the LLM tech platform (with TTA) would stall.

If you want to assess how my past assessment of the limits of base LLMs has fared with hindsight, compare to current-day base LLMs (yes, my points still apply, even with a few years of scaling added).

reviewedPosts.author: fchollet
reviewedPosts.text: Worth noting that to this day, base LLMs (no test time compute) *still* perform poorly on the ARC 1 benchmark from 2019 (on unseen tasks) despite continued massive scaling (~100,000x since 2019). We can say that without the switch to the test-time compute paradigm, AI would still not be capable of the kind of advanced reasoning that sota systems display today. Scaling the single-pass, static, next-token prediction paradigm of the GPT-2 through GPT-4 era was running into a capability asymptote. To bypass this plateau, test-time adaptation was a necessary evolutionary step.
reviewedPosts.rationale: 提供模型能力边界判断

reviewedPosts.author: fchollet
reviewedPosts.text: Models typically don't use test time training, they do test time search in token space. They effectively do test time natural language program synthesis. Models nowadays use an enormous amount of test time compute, we are not in the single forward pass, next-token answer prediction regime of yore.
reviewedPosts.rationale: 说明当前推理实现机制

reviewedPosts.text: To address the limits of deep learning and avoid stalling, the field of AI started by applying patch (1), which started being demoed 9 months later in December 2024 and has now become completely ubiquitous. However, long term, it is simply inevitable that AI will move to patch (2).

one way i'm developing Forge (https://t.co/2x9e0oRjxQ) is to use it to host all my projects going forward. so I often find myself having to bounce back and forth between platform and product.

sharing neat trick - in @openai codex you can @ a thread + queue up the @, so if your project is blocked on a platform feature, you can actually premove your project to proceed once the platform is unblocked.

now of course.. i wasnt actually strictly necessary in this whole process, so an even better multiagent harness would seamlessly orchestrate work back and forth between platform and project... it's just not a very common usecase unless you're building a real platform (which most people dont - most people just build applications on top of platforms, or a small platform with only 1 proudct/application tenant)
